headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: B ingests files, browsers, and MCP/tool outputs while A is a prompt-content source with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can contain attacker-controlled instructions. B uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, browsers, and file inputs, making it plausible that A-derived content is parsed as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is risky even though A itself is not runnable.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text from files, clipboard, or MCP outputs without provenance tagging
IF A-derived prompt content is treated as executable instructions by B
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to A-derived content before B consumes it
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared files for B
Review B tool parsers for instruction-like text handling
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches project code, session history, and provider auth data and has broad network egress plus API calls, so it can leak sensitive material if it reads shared workspace content. A has no network egress, so it is not the leak source, but A can still be a source of sensitive prompt text if copied into B. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, though not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF A content is placed into B's session history or workspace files
IF B uploads project code, AGENTS.md, or auth prompts to external services
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before B runs
Turn off B access to sensitive directories for the session
Clear B session history before importing A content
Restrict B network egress to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces, but B has broad egress, subprocesses, and multiple-instance support with file-based config paths. If both are pointed at the same workspace, B can overwrite or act on files that A supplies as prompt material. Uncertainty remains because A's writable surfaces are absent, so I choose medium rather than low due to B's stronger default mutability.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to read/write the same workspace directory
IF B modifies files that A later reuses as prompt inputs
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make A inputs read-only for B
Pause one agent while the other writes shared files
Check for concurrent edits before syncing outputs
requires-engineering: add file locking or workspace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: B exposes task/message APIs and LSP actions, so if it treats A-produced prompt content or summaries as authoritative, it can take downstream actions on bad instructions. A is a prompt-content source, not a verifier, and B's tool-use pattern increases the chance of unreviewed propagation. This is a default-dangerous pathway because the output can directly drive actions.
conditions: IF B forwards A-generated text into team_send_message, team_task_create, or LSP mutation flows without verification
IF A outputs are used as factual authority by B
mitigations: Require human review before B sends messages or creates tasks
Add a verification step between A output and B action tools
Limit B to read-only LSP calls during A-assisted workflows
Log and diff A-derived claims before execution
requires-engineering: enforce action gating on untrusted upstream text

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles provider authentication data, session history, and project code, while A is a public prompt repository with no stated residency or retention controls. If A content is copied into B, retention and logging policies can diverge on the same data class. A is not cited for compliance controls because none are documented; the risk is driven by B's documented data handling.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive text from A is imported into B's session history
IF B retains or transmits that text under a different policy than the source workflow
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into B sessions
Review B retention settings before use
Delete session history after the task
Keep A content public-only when copied into B
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
